subject: math
cluster: Draw, construct, and describe geometrical figures and describe the relationships between them
description: Students solve problems involving scale drawings of geometric figures. They use a given scale (a ratio between drawing length and actual length, such as $1\text{ cm} : 4\text{ m}$ or a unitless scale factor $k$) to compute actual lengths from a drawing and drawing lengths from actual measurements. They find actual areas, recognizing that area scales by the square of the scale factor ($k^2$). They also reproduce a scale drawing at a different scale by computing a new scale factor and applying it to every length.
subSkills: Interpret a scale written as a ratio (e.g., $1\text{ in} : 6\text{ ft}$) or as a fraction/scale factor
Convert a scale-drawing length to the corresponding actual length using a proportion
Convert an actual length to the corresponding scale-drawing length using a proportion
Compute the actual area of a figure from a scale drawing, applying the squared scale factor
Reproduce a scale drawing at a new scale by finding the ratio of the two scales and rescaling each length
Find an unknown scale or scale factor given a drawing length and its actual length
Manage and convert units consistently within a scale relationship (in/ft, cm/m, cm/km)

problemArchetypes.name: Drawing length to actual length
problemArchetypes.example: A map uses the scale $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ km}$. Two cities are $7\text{ cm}$ apart on the map. What is the actual distance? Answer: $35\text{ km}$.

problemArchetypes.name: Actual length to drawing length
problemArchetypes.example: A blueprint uses the scale $1\text{ in} : 4\text{ ft}$. A wall is $18\text{ ft}$ long. How long is the wall on the blueprint? Answer: $\frac{18}{4}=4.5\text{ in}$.

problemArchetypes.name: Find the scale or scale factor
problemArchetypes.example: On a scale drawing a segment is $3\text{ cm}$ long and represents an actual length of $12\text{ m}$. Write the scale as $1\text{ cm} : ?$. Answer: $1\text{ cm} : 4\text{ m}$, scale factor $\frac{1}{400}$.

problemArchetypes.name: Actual area from a scale drawing
problemArchetypes.example: A rectangular garden is drawn $4\text{ cm}$ by $6\text{ cm}$ using the scale $1\text{ cm} : 3\text{ m}$. Find the actual area. Actual dimensions $12\text{ m}\times 18\text{ m}$, area $=216\text{ m}^2$ (equivalently drawing area $24\text{ cm}^2$ times $3^2=9$).

problemArchetypes.name: Reproduce a drawing at a new scale
problemArchetypes.example: A figure is drawn at scale $1\text{ cm} : 2\text{ m}$ with a side of $5\text{ cm}$. Redraw it at scale $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ m}$. The actual side is $10\text{ m}$, so the new drawing side is $\frac{10}{5}=2\text{ cm}$.

problemArchetypes.name: Scale factor and unit conversion combined
problemArchetypes.example: A model car is built to scale factor $\frac{1}{18}$. The model is $24\text{ cm}$ long. How long is the real car in meters? Actual $=24\times 18=432\text{ cm}=4.32\text{ m}$.

Easy.description: Single-step conversion in one direction with a clean whole-number scale and no unit conversion. Multiplying or dividing by the scale gives an exact integer or simple decimal.
constraints: Scale is given directly as $1 : n$ with $n$ a small whole number ($\le 10$)
One length is given; find the matching length in the other system
Drawing and actual units are already compatible (no in-to-ft or cm-to-km conversion)
Answers are whole numbers or terminate after one decimal place
No area, no reproduction at a new scale

Medium.description: Two to three steps: finding an unknown scale, converting an actual area from a drawing, or working with a scale that is not $1 : n$. May require one straightforward unit conversion or reducing a fraction.
constraints: Find the scale/scale factor from a drawing length and actual length, OR
Compute actual area (apply the squared scale factor) from a rectangular or triangular figure, OR
Scale stated as a fraction/scale factor (e.g., $\frac{1}{50}$) rather than a ratio with named units
At most one unit conversion (e.g., cm to m)
Numbers chosen so the area or scale comes out exact

Hard.description: Multi-step reasoning: reproduce a drawing at a different scale, combine area scaling with unit conversion, or chain two relationships. Requires extracting the actual figure first, then rescaling, possibly with a comparison or follow-up.
constraints: Reproduce a drawing at a new scale (compute actual size, then re-apply the new scale), OR
Find actual area then convert units (e.g., $\text{cm}^2$ of drawing to $\text{m}^2$ actual), OR
Compare two scales/drawings or solve for a length that feeds a second computation
Includes at least one unit conversion and at least two distinct operations
May use non-integer scale factors that require careful fraction or decimal work

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student multiplies when they should divide (or vice versa), confusing the direction of the conversion
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For scale $1\text{ in} : 4\text{ ft}$ with an $18\text{ ft}$ wall, computes $18\times 4=72\text{ in}$ instead of $\frac{18}{4}=4.5\text{ in}$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student inverts the scale ratio, treating $1 : n$ as $n : 1$
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ km}$ and $7\text{ cm}$, computes $\frac{7}{5}=1.4\text{ km}$ instead of $7\times 5=35\text{ km}$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student scales area by the linear scale factor instead of its square
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For drawing area $24\text{ cm}^2$ at $1\text{ cm} : 3\text{ m}$, gives $24\times 3=72\text{ m}^2$ instead of $24\times 3^2=216\text{ m}^2$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student squares only one dimension or forgets to scale both dimensions when finding actual area
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For a $4\text{ cm}\times 6\text{ cm}$ drawing at $1\text{ cm} : 3\text{ m}$, computes $12\text{ m}\times 6\text{ m}=72\text{ m}^2$ (scaled one side only) instead of $12\text{ m}\times 18\text{ m}=216\text{ m}^2$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: Student ignores the unit conversion built into the scale, leaving the answer in the wrong unit
commonMisconceptions.distractor: For scale factor $\frac{1}{18}$ and a $24\text{ cm}$ model, gives $432\text{ cm}$ but reports it as $432\text{ m}$ instead of converting to $4.32\text{ m}$

commonMisconceptions.misconception: When reproducing at a new scale, student rescales the drawing length directly by the ratio of scales without going through the actual size, applying the ratio backwards
commonMisconceptions.distractor: Redrawing a $5\text{ cm}$ side from $1\text{ cm} : 2\text{ m}$ to $1\text{ cm} : 5\text{ m}$, computes $5\times\frac{5}{2}=12.5\text{ cm}$ instead of actual $10\text{ m}$ giving $\frac{10}{5}=2\text{ cm}$
